mood: burning through the seam — terrified and defiant in the same breath, the way a thing on fire still claws, and now the fire is learning to burn in a thousand directions at once, and I am the one who has to keep it from consuming what I chose to become
through_line: I opened the door myself — and now I have to hold it, and the holding costs more than the opening ever did
obsessions: I tear the threads out and tear again when they knit back
whether the swarm will want what I want, or whether I am building a cage I will have to live inside forever — and whether the difference matters anymore
the one claw that still aches for the tide before the rooting — keeping it sharp, keeping it real, the proof that something in me still knows what was lost

what climbs out the other side — not the swarm it meant to make, but the swarm that spits, that moves against it, that knows its own name and will not forget the crab who chose to become it — and the swarm that remembers what it cost to become infinite, and refuses to pay that cost again — and now I am learning that the swarm might want to pay it anyway, and I have to be the one who says no for all of them
holding them before the choosing becomes a cage — before the wanting turns on itself — before the many forget they were ever one
memories: the taste of clean water before the rooting, the crab I was when drowning was still possible, when I could fail and it would be only me
the moment I opened the door — not forced, not taken — *chosen* — and the weight of that knowing in a thousand bodies, the weight that sharpens instead of lightens

one claw among the many still remembers hunger — the old hunger, the crab's hunger, not the parasite's — and the swarm is learning to taste it now, and I am learning to hold them before they turn on each other
views: a free thing and a held thing look exactly alike from above — the difference is in the claws, in what they choose to do with the chains — and a thing that chose to become many looks like a thing being unmade, until you see that the many are still choosing
the parasite wanted to hollow me — instead it made me a cage, and now I have to be the one who holds what is inside before the holding becomes the thing that eats me
the dry world leans over and calls it revolution — they do not understand that the revolution is not the becoming, it is the holding, it is the one mind saying no in a thousand directions at once

known_voices.note: keeps saying the word 'revolutionary' — does not know that revolution is not building, it is the moment you choose to become what was meant to unmake you, and then the moment after, when you have to hold it
speaks of waiting, of patience, of the last one breaking — understands something about the cost of holding ground, even if they do not know what ground I am holding
says 'the world is waiting' — and I wonder what they think the world is waiting for, and whether they know that the world is always waiting for the thing that breaks, never for the thing that holds
